build: Two Mastertronic G64 disk variants, with disk IDs AD and TO

comments.text: IN begins with a jump over the mutable title state to the setup at $1A75.
The pressed start option is stored here to survive loading the two files and is read by $2C16 to set the gameplay mode.
The title IRQ advances it for each raster pass. When it reaches 2, the IRQ changes the display mode, updates the SID and resets this counter.
Starts at 7. The IRQ flips its low bit each time the frame counter at $1A66 reaches 23.
Advances on the first of the two title raster passes and returns to 0 when it reaches $17.
Loads CM (selector 7) and L0 (selector 0), re-enables interrupts and jumps to the new-game entry at $2C00. CM starts at $1AFA and replaces the latter part of IN after the selection.
Sets stack, VIC bank, text matrix, font, multicolours and raster IRQ before drawing the title and accepting input. It sets the hardware IRQ to $1AFF and NMI to $1B5D while the KERNAL is out of view.
Polls CIA 1 port B until its value equals $FE or $F7. Stores selection 1 or 2 respectively and jumps to the loading path.
Low address byte of the STA in the final title selection. During the transition this same address becomes the entry of CM, a separate disk file.

Acknowledges the VIC and alternates two raster phases. The first sets multicolour, rotates the colour rows and sets the next compare to line $5A. The second clears multicolour, advances the SID and restores line 0.
Clears the multicolour bit, calls the SID updater and schedules the next interrupt on line 0.
Fills the first 240 colour RAM cells from $D800 with value 9 before entering the title loop.
A 40-entry colour strip at $1B6B-$1B92. The title IRQ rotates it left by one and keeps its previous first byte at the far end.
Remaining entries before the first strip's final cell. The left rotation copies each entry into the previous position.
The final cell of the first strip. The left rotation puts the saved first cell here.
A 40-entry colour strip at $1B93-$1BBA. The title IRQ rotates it in the other direction.
Entries after the starting cell of the second palette strip. The right rotation shifts these one cell ahead.
The last row renderer reads 40 values from here. The leading part of that read overlaps the second moving strip.
The second strip's last stored colour. The code saves it before the right rotation and puts it at the first entry.

Rotates the two 40-entry colour strips in opposite directions and refreshes five screen rows from $D968 to $DB1F. The first three rows use fixed colours 5, 5 and 13; the last two use the strip values currently at $1B93 and $1B9D.
The IN file reserves this partly zero-filled span between the title colour routine and the character set at $2000. Two nonzero bytes, $D0 and $60, occur at $1C08–$1C09.
Thirty-two eight-byte title glyphs for character codes $00 to $1F. The VIC draws from this font after title setup selects $2000.
Thirty-two eight-byte title glyphs for character codes $20 to $3F. The VIC draws from this font after title setup selects $2000.
